nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What methodology did Qamruzzaman and Jianguo use in their study regarding renewable energy and trade openness?
nodes.answer: They used a panel nonlinear ARDL model covering the years from 1990 to 2017.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What percentage of global electricity production is projected for renewable energy by mid-century?
nodes.answer: Renewable energy is expected to account for 50% of global electricity production by mid-century.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How is the average renewable penetration increase calculated over a 10-year period?
nodes.answer: The average renewable penetration increase is determined by evaluating the difference in renewable energy penetration over two consecutive years for 10 years from 2009 to 2,018 as per EQ. (2), and then averaging these values.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What method does the proposed forecasting model utilize for the analysis of carbon prices?
nodes.answer: The proposed forecasting model utilizes a hybrid feature-driven framework that includes decomposition, reconstruction, prediction, and ensemble.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which techniques are used in the forecasting model to predict carbon price series?
nodes.answer: The forecasting model uses Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) for decomposition, Sample Entropy (SE) for reconstruction, and Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for prediction.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_005
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How does the performance of the proposed forecasting model compare to existing benchmark models?
nodes.answer: The empirical results show that the proposed model performs more efficiently than the current benchmark models.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is there an interest in modelling and forecasting GHG emissions?
nodes.answer: The interest in modelling and forecasting GHG emissions arises from the need to ensure that energy policies are as effective as possible and to understand the main dynamics and drivers of emissions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is a combination of econometric and machine learning models often used in carbon price forecasting?
nodes.answer: A combination of econometric and machine learning models is used because carbon prices are non-linear and non-stationary, allowing econometric models to predict the linear part and machine learning models to predict the non-linear part effectively.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Clean energy integration|Renewable energy forecasting_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What hybrid forecasting method did Zhang and Wu (2022) propose for carbon price prediction in the EU ETS?
nodes.answer: Zhang and Wu (2022) proposed a hybrid forecasting method that incorporates empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and the integration of ARMAs and LSSVMs.
